title: Alchemy
content: Alchemy creates potions, elixirs and flasks from herbs. You need Herbalism or the Auction House for materials. Trainers are in every major city. Potions heal or restore mana; elixirs and flasks give temporary stat boosts for raiding.

title: Blacksmithing
content: Blacksmithing makes plate armor and melee weapons, plus sharpening stones and some keys. It uses ore and bars from Mining. Trainers are in every major city and most towns.

title: Enchanting
content: Enchanting adds permanent stat bonuses to your gear and can disenchant unwanted items into dusts, essences and shards used for enchanting. It needs no gathering profession, just unwanted gear. Trainers are in major cities.

title: Engineering
content: Engineering crafts gadgets, explosives, goggles and mechanical items. It is powerful but sometimes random or unreliable. It uses ore and cloth. Goggles and trinkets are highly desired. Trainers are in major cities.

title: Tailoring
content: Tailoring makes cloth armor and bags, and some special cloths. It uses cloth drops from humanoids. Bags are always in demand. Trainers are in major cities.

title: Leatherworking
content: Leatherworking makes leather and mail armor, plus armor kits. It uses leather from Skinning. Druids, hunters, rogues and shamans benefit most. Trainers are in major cities.

title: Jewelcrafting
content: Jewelcrafting cuts gems that socket into gear and crafts rings, necklaces and trinkets. It uses ores to prospect into gems. Introduced in The Burning Crusade; trainers are in Shattrath and major cities.

title: Inscription
content: Inscription creates glyphs that modify your spells and abilities, plus scrolls and off-hand items. It uses herbs to mill into pigments. Introduced in Wrath of the Lich King; trainers are in major cities.

title: Herbalism
content: Herbalism lets you gather herbs from nodes found in the world, used by Alchemy and Inscription. Herbs appear on your minimap once you learn the skill. Trainers are in major cities.

title: Mining
content: Mining lets you gather ore from mineral veins, used by Blacksmithing, Engineering and Jewelcrafting. Veins appear on your minimap once you learn the skill. Trainers are in major cities.

title: Skinning
content: Skinning lets you skin leather from dead beasts, used by Leatherworking. You can also get scraps and occasionally meat. Trainers are in major cities.

title: Cooking
content: Cooking is a secondary profession (everyone can learn it) that turns meat and fish into food that restores health and grants temporary stat buffs. Trainers are in major cities and many towns.

title: First Aid
content: First Aid is a secondary profession (everyone can learn it) that bandages you mid-combat to restore health. It uses cloth. Trainers are in major cities.

title: Fishing
content: Fishing is a secondary profession (everyone can learn it) that catches fish from water, used for Cooking or sold. It is slow but relaxing. Trainers are in major cities.

title: Warrior
content: Warriors are melee fighters who wear plate armor and can tank or deal damage. They use rage as a resource, generated by dealing and taking damage. They are slow to level but very durable.

title: Paladin
content: Paladins are holy warriors who wear plate and can tank, heal or deal damage. They use mana and have powerful auras and blessings. They can wear plate from level 40.

title: Hunter
content: Hunters are ranged damage dealers who tame and fight alongside a pet. They wear mail and use a bow or gun. Pets can tank for them while leveling, making hunters easy to solo with.

title: Rogue
content: Rogues are stealthy melee damage dealers who wear leather and use energy plus combo points. They can pick locks and vanish. They are excellent at burst damage and crowd control.

title: Priest
content: Priests are healers or shadow damage dealers who wear cloth and use mana. Holy priests are among the best healers; shadow priests deal damage over time.

title: Death Knight
content: Death Knights are hero class available from level 55. They wear plate and use runes and runic power. They can tank or deal damage.

title: Shaman
content: Shamans wear mail and use totems to buff allies or damage enemies. They can heal, deal melee damage or cast elemental damage. They use mana.

title: Mage
content: Mages are ranged damage dealers who wear cloth and use mana. They have powerful area damage, crowd control, and can conjure food, water and portals.

title: Warlock
content: Warlocks are ranged damage dealers who wear cloth and command demons. They use mana and soul shards, and can summon allies and healthstones.

title: Druid
content: Druids are versatile shapeshifters who wear leather and can tank (bear), deal melee damage (cat), heal, or cast spells. They can shapeshift at level 10 and are excellent soloers.

title: Ground mounts
content: You learn riding at level 20 (75% speed) for a few gold, and again at level 40 (100% speed). Mounts are bought from your race's mount vendor. Paladins and warlocks get class mounts for free.

title: Flying mounts
content: Flying is available in Outland and Northrend. Learn flying at level 60 (Outland) and cold weather flying at level 77 (Northrend). You must buy the flying license from a trainer.

title: Talents
content: You gain talent points starting at level 10, one per level. Talents are spent in three trees to specialize. Dual specialization can be bought at level 40 from your class trainer.

title: Earning gold
content: Earn gold by questing, selling loot and gathered materials on the Auction House, and doing daily quests. Professions like mining, herbalism and skinning sell well. Don't buy every skill rank you don't need.

title: Auction House
content: The Auction House lets you buy and sell items with other players. It is in every capital city. Gathered materials (ore, herbs, leather, cloth) usually sell well. Check prices before selling.

title: Bank
content: Banks store your items and gold. Visit a banker in any major city to deposit items you don't need to carry. You can buy extra bag slots.

title: Flight paths
content: Flight masters let you fly between discovered locations for a small fee. Discover new flight points by visiting towns and talking to their flight master.

title: Hearthstone
content: Your Hearthstone teleports you back to the inn you are bound to. Talk to an innkeeper to set your home location. It has a 30 minute cooldown.

title: Dungeon level ranges
content: Dungeons are 5-player group content at set level ranges: Ragefire Chasm and Deadmines around level 15-20, Scarlet Monastery around 30-40, Scholomance and Stratholme around 55-60, and Northrend dungeons at 70-80.

title: Raids
content: Raids are large-group content for 10 or 25 players. Classic raids include Molten Core, Blackwing Lair and Ahn'Qiraj; Burning Crusade raids include Karazhan; Wrath raids include Naxxramas, Ulduar and Icecrown Citadel.

title: Zone level ranges
content: Zones scale by level. Starter zones are 1-10, then Barrens/Westfall/Darkshore 10-20, Stranglethorn and Hillsbrad 30-40, Tanaris and Feralas 40-50, Un'Goro and Felwood 50-60, then Outland 60-70 and Northrend 70-80.

title: Dual specialization
content: Dual specialization lets you keep two talent builds and swap between them. Buy it at level 40 from your class trainer for 1000 gold.

title: Learning professions
content: To learn a profession, find a profession trainer in a major city and ask a guard for directions. You can have two primary professions and all three secondary ones (Cooking, First Aid, Fishing).

title: Deadmines
content: Deadmines is a 5-player dungeon in Westfall for levels 15-22. It is in the Defias brotherhood's mine and ends with the boss Edwin VanCleef. Good early gear and the Defias questline rewards.

title: Scarlet Monastery
content: Scarlet Monastery is a 4-wing dungeon in Tirisfal Glades for levels 30-40. It has good cloth and caster gear, plus the famous Scarlet Crusade lore. Wings: Graveyard, Library, Armory, Cathedral.

title: Stratholme
content: Stratholme is a 5-player dungeon in the Eastern Plaguelands for levels 55-60. It is the ruined city from the Third War, filled with undead. Baron Rivendare drops the rare Deathcharger mount.

title: Utgarde Keep
content: Utgarde Keep is a 5-player dungeon in Howling Fjord, Northrend, for levels 70-72. It is the first dungeon most players do in Wrath of the Lich King.

title: Elwynn Forest
content: Elwynn Forest is the human starter zone for levels 1-10, around Stormwind. Peaceful woods, farms and the Defias threat.

title: Westfall
content: Westfall is a level 10-20 zone south of Elwynn, known for its farms, the Defias brotherhood and the Deadmines.

title: The Barrens
content: The Barrens is a large Horde zone for levels 10-25, known for its savanna, quillboars and the Wailing Caverns. It is a classic Horde leveling zone.

title: Stranglethorn Vale
content: Stranglethorn Vale is a level 30-45 jungle zone known for trolls, pirates, and the Booty Bay goblin town. It has many PvP encounters.

title: Bags
content: Bags expand your inventory. You start with a 16-slot backpack and can equip four extra bags. Bigger bags (14-18 slots) are crafted by tailors or bought at the Auction House.

title: Reputation
content: Reputation tracks your standing with factions, from Hated to Exalted. Earn it through quests and kills. High reputation unlocks special rewards, discounts and mounts.

title: Rest XP
content: Rest XP doubles experience from kills while you are logged out in an inn or capital city. It builds up over time. Log out in an inn to earn it.

title: Battlegrounds
content: Battlegrounds are PvP arenas like Warsong Gulch (10-19 and up), Arathi Basin, and Alterac Valley. Join from the PvP menu. They reward honor points and marks.

title: Glyphs
content: Glyphs modify your spells and abilities. You unlock glyph slots at level 15, 30, 50, 70 and 80. Glyphs are made by Scribes (Inscription).

title: Daily quests
content: Daily quests are repeatable quests that reset every day and reward gold, reputation or tokens. They are marked with a blue exclamation mark and appear at level 70 in Outland and Northrend.
